newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mortgage-backeds stagger in late trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mortgage-backeds stagger in late trade.

text.p: A short-lived buying spree jolted U.S. mortgage-backed securities higher, but sellers quickly moved in and pushed pass-throughs lower by late afternoon Thursday, market sources said.
Pass-throughs were largely unchanged earlier in the day, but gathered fuel midday as buyers saw good deals in premium coupons, they said.
"We've been buying some 8.5 (percent) paper," said one New York-based trader, but added the recent gains may soon recede as mortgages become better offered.
Indeed, discount coupons rose as high as 6/32 before sellers rolled in, pushing prices 2/32 lower.
Attractive prices lured dealers to the market, said another trader.
"Ginnie's have been cheap all along and all it takes is just one big dealer (to stir things up)," he said.
"The biggest exposed focus right now is on Ginnie Mae 7.5's and Fannie Mae 8.5's," he said.
The trader also noted many dealers have been playing dollar rolls.
For example, an institution sells a security held in its portfolio to a dealer and agrees to repurchase a substantially indentical security on a future date at a specified price.
In late trading, pass-throughs were 1/32 to 2/32 lower in current and discount coupons and were unchanged in premium coupons.

Specifically, Ginnie Mae 30-year pass-throughs were off 2/32 to 99-01/32, yielding 105 basis points over the 10-year Treasury note. Comparable Fannie Mae 7.5 percent coupons were down 1/32 to 100-26/32, and Freddie Mac 7.0s were 2/32 lower at 99-02/32.
